newsitem.title: USA: U.S. destroys mines around its naval base in Cuba.
newsitem.headline: U.S. destroys mines around its naval base in Cuba.

text.p: U.S. Marines are blowing up landmines around the U.S. Guantanamo Bay Naval Base in Cuba, expecting to destroy the last of them by the end of 1999, a Defence Department spokesman said on Thursday.
"This is a part of a multi-year programme to explode ageing mines down there at Guantanamo Bay in Cuba," the spokesman, Capt. Michael Doubleday said.

The landmines were originally planted around the U.S. base on the southeastern tip of the Communist-ruled island to prevent an attack. The base will continue to have Marine guards and fences around its perimeter.

President Bill Clinton last year ordered the destruction of all U.S. anti-personnel landmines except those used for the defence of South Korea. A spokesman for the U.S. Atlantic Fleet at Norfolk, Virginia, said the process started last May at Guantanamo.

A State Department official said there were probably thousands of landmines in the stretch of land separating the base from Cuban territory. The base, leased to the United States since the beginning of the century, was once an important training and maintenance facility. More recently, it was used to house refugees fleeing from Haiti and Cuba.

Cuba's Communist government, which maintains that the United States has been occupying Guantanamo illegally since 1903, has its own minefield around the base. Cuba has never attacked Guantanamo but some Cubans seeking refuge have been wounded by landmines while trying to get to the base.
